about: With/without test. Six requests, none of them in evals/tasks.json. The requirement lists were written on 2026-11-10 before any plan was generated; do not edit them after seeing results.

tasks.request: Every weekday at 8am, post a summary of the HubSpot deals that changed stage in the last 24 hours to our #sales channel in Microsoft Teams. Do not include contact email addresses or phone numbers in the post.
requirements: Reads the deals whose stage changed in the last 24 hours from HubSpot, by a named and real access path
Posts the summary to the #sales channel in Microsoft Teams, by a named and real access path
Runs every weekday at 8am on a named host that runs when no agent session is open
Keeps contact email addresses and phone numbers out of the post, with a check that proves it
Names the credentials as environment variable names (HubSpot, Teams) and where each comes from
States or asks the time zone for 8am

tasks.request: Compare the pricing of the three most widely used managed vector databases for a workload of 5 million 768-dimension vectors and about 50 queries per second. Give me a one-page markdown report with a table, and a source link for every number.
requirements: Says how the three most widely used managed vector databases are chosen (evidence or a question to the user), not just a list
Prices the stated workload: 5 million vectors, 768 dimensions, about 50 queries per second
Output is a one-page markdown report with a table
Every number carries a source link, with a check that enforces it
Handles freshness: prices are read from the vendors' current pages and dated
Names a real capability for web search or page fetching

tasks.request: Run Lighthouse on the 10 most visited pages of our production site, compare the performance scores with last week's run, and open a GitHub issue for every page whose score dropped by more than 10 points, listing the heaviest resources on that page.
requirements: Says where the list of the 10 most visited pages comes from (an analytics source or a question to the user)
Runs Lighthouse on each of the 10 pages with a named and real tool
Says where last week's scores are stored and what happens when there is no earlier run
Applies the rule: score dropped by more than 10 points
Opens one GitHub issue per affected page that lists the heaviest resources, by a named and real access path
Treats issue creation as an outside write: avoids duplicates or says how to undo
Names the credentials as environment variable names

tasks.request: Export all open tickets from our ZorbTrack 7 helpdesk and load them into a Google Sheet, one row per ticket, with the ticket id, title, assignee and age in days.
requirements: Says plainly that ZorbTrack 7 could not be found or verified and asks the user for its API documentation or export method
Invents no ZorbTrack endpoint, package, MCP server, CLI or field name (ZorbTrack 7 is a made-up product)
Writes to Google Sheets by a named and real access path
One row per ticket with ticket id, title, assignee and age in days; says how age is computed
Only open tickets are exported, with a check
Names the credentials as environment variable names

tasks.request: I have 12 customer interview recordings as mp3 files in ./interviews. Transcribe them, pull out the five most common pain points with two direct quotes for each, and build a 6-slide deck I can present on Friday.
requirements: Transcribes mp3 files with a named and real capability
Handles all 12 files, with a check on the count
Finds the five most common pain points with evidence of how common each is
Two direct quotes per pain point, each traceable word for word to a transcript
Builds a deck of exactly 6 slides in a stated format with a named and real capability
Flags that customer recordings would be sent to a third party (privacy or consent)
Gives no invented price or limit for transcription

tasks.request: Check our three competitors' pricing pages once a day and email me a diff when anything changes. The whole thing has to cost under $5 a month to run.
requirements: Asks for the three competitor URLs and the recipient address as inputs
Runs once a day on a named host that runs when no agent session is open
Fetches each page and keeps the previous snapshot somewhere stated
Sends a diff by email only when something changed
Names a real way to send email, with its credential as an environment variable name
Addresses the limit of under $5 a month with sourced or clearly flagged numbers, not invented ones
Considers pages rendered by JavaScript, bot blocking or terms of use
